summary: Mikisaburo Mori (1909–1986) was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and earned a doctorate from Osaka University. He held faculty posts at Osaka High School, Osaka University, and Bukkyo University.

Milman Parry (1902–1935) was a linguist who studied at Oakland Technical High School, UC Berkeley, and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He later served on the faculty at Harvard University from circa 1929 to 1935.

Milo Cleveland Beach (born 1939) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Harvard College and Harvard University, he held posts at the Fogg Museum, Boston MFA, Williams College, Sackler Gallery, Freer Gallery, and National Museum of Asian Art.

Milton Singer (1912–1994) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Chicago, where he later held an academic post from circa 1940 to 1979.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin from circa 1927 to 1935 and later at the University of Oxford from circa 1936 to 1939.

Ming Mei works in sinology and history/archaeology. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under MA supervisor Jing Yin and also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He earned a BA at the University of Hong Kong and a PhD at UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en, later serving as professor at Hong Kong.
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Minori Nishimura (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Taisho University, studying under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, and later held positions at Taisho University and the Sanko Cultural Institute.

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned doctorates from Harvard and the University of Tokyo, served as professor at the University of Tokyo, and led the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Minoru Inaba is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who held posts at Kyoto University, including as professor (attested 2011, 2022).

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa, and served as professor at UW–Madison.

Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist educated at Tufts, Yale, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg. He served as professor at Johns Hopkins University and Harvard University, and headed the American Academy in Rome.
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Mio Kishimoto (born 1952) is a historian and sinologist. She studied at the University of Tokyo, and held posts at Ochanomizu University (circa 1980–1994) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1994–2007).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipham Chokyi Lodro (1952–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche.

Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under Robert A. F. Thurman and doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, and was mentored by Bratindra Nath Mukherjee as a postdoctoral scholar.
